questions.question: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is a:

options.B: Layer 2 protocol that prevents loops in a switched network

questions.explanation: STP works at Layer 2 and blocks redundant paths so that a switched network does not form loops.

questions.question: The root bridge in STP is the switch with the:
questions.explanation: The switch with the lowest Bridge ID (priority plus MAC address) is elected as the root bridge.

questions.question: BPDU stands for:
questions.explanation: Switches exchange Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) to run STP.

questions.question: PortFast allows a port to:

options.D: Go to the forwarding state straight away

questions.explanation: PortFast skips the listening and learning states so the port goes to forwarding immediately.

questions.question: PortFast should be enabled only on ports connected to:

options.C: End devices such as PCs, servers and printers

questions.explanation: End devices cannot create Layer 2 loops, so PortFast is safe only on ports facing them.

questions.question: BPDU Guard puts a PortFast port into the err-disabled state when it:
questions.explanation: A BPDU arriving on a PortFast port suggests a switch has been connected, so BPDU Guard shuts the port down.

questions.question: UplinkFast recovers from a link failure in about:
questions.explanation: UplinkFast switches to the backup uplink in about 5 seconds, instead of the roughly 45 seconds normal STP needs.

questions.question: BackboneFast helps recovery from:
questions.explanation: BackboneFast speeds up STP convergence after an indirect link failure elsewhere in the network.

questions.question: The default Max Age timer in STP is:
questions.explanation: The default Max Age timer is 20 seconds.

questions.question: RLQ in BackboneFast stands for:
questions.explanation: RLQ is the Root Link Query that a switch sends to check whether the path to the root is still available.

questions.question: Quality of Service (QoS) is used to:

options.D: Give priority to important types of traffic

questions.explanation: QoS classifies traffic so that important traffic gets priority over less important traffic.

questions.question: The biggest reason for using QoS is:
questions.explanation: VoIP is delay and jitter sensitive, so it is the main reason QoS is needed.

questions.question: The voice (RTP) stream of VoIP uses which transport protocol?
questions.explanation: The RTP voice stream runs over UDP to avoid the overhead and delay of TCP.

questions.question: HTTP is based on:
questions.explanation: HTTP runs over TCP, which provides reliable delivery.

questions.question: The TOS (Type of Service) field is part of the:
questions.explanation: The TOS field is an 8-bit field in the IP header.

questions.question: The first 3 bits of the 8-bit TOS field indicate the:
questions.explanation: The first 3 bits of the TOS field carry the IP precedence value.

questions.question: Low Latency Queuing (LLQ) is a:
questions.explanation: LLQ adds a strict priority queue, usually used for voice, that is always served first.

questions.question: WFQ stands for:
questions.explanation: WFQ is Weighted Fair Queuing, which serves queues according to their weights.

questions.question: The Leaky Bucket algorithm gives:
questions.explanation: The leaky bucket releases packets at a fixed rate, which smooths bursty input into constant output.

questions.question: The Token Bucket algorithm allows:
questions.explanation: Saved tokens let the token bucket send bursts of traffic.

questions.question: Jitter is:
questions.explanation: Jitter is the variation in delay between packets.

questions.question: Latency (delay) is:

options.C: The time a packet takes to travel from source to destination

questions.explanation: Latency is the time a packet takes to travel from source to destination.

questions.question: Bandwidth is a link's ability to:

options.D: Transmit the maximum amount of data in a specific time

questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum amount of data a link can transmit in a given time.

questions.question: A routing protocol is used by routers to:

options.B: Exchange information about the state of the network

questions.explanation: Routers use routing protocols to share network information and build their routing tables.

questions.question: A floating static route is used as a:
questions.explanation: A floating static route has a higher administrative distance and is used only as a backup when the main route fails.

questions.question: The metric used by RIP is:
questions.explanation: RIP uses hop count as its metric.

questions.question: The metric used by OSPF is:
questions.explanation: OSPF calculates cost from the link bandwidth.

questions.question: The default metrics of EIGRP are:
questions.explanation: By default EIGRP uses bandwidth and delay to compute its metric.

questions.question: The administrative distance with the lower value is:
questions.explanation: A lower administrative distance means the route source is more trusted.

questions.question: The administrative distance of OSPF (as per notes) is:
questions.explanation: The administrative distance of OSPF is 110.

questions.question: The administrative distance of RIP is:
questions.explanation: The administrative distance of RIP is 120.

questions.question: Which are examples of IGPs?
questions.explanation: RIP, EIGRP and OSPF work inside an autonomous system, so they are IGPs.

questions.question: Which is an example of an EGP?
questions.explanation: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol used between autonomous systems.

questions.question: RIP broadcasts all its routes every:
questions.explanation: RIP sends its full routing table every 30 seconds.

questions.question: EIGRP is described as a:
questions.explanation: EIGRP combines distance vector and link state features, so it is called a hybrid protocol.

questions.question: OSPF is a:
questions.explanation: OSPF routers share link states and build a topology map, which makes it a link state protocol.

questions.question: The OSPF backbone area is:
questions.explanation: Area 0 is the OSPF backbone area.

questions.question: An Area Border Router (ABR) resides in:
questions.explanation: An ABR has interfaces in more than one area and connects them.

questions.question: The DR generates which LSA?
questions.explanation: The Designated Router generates the Type 2 Network LSA for the multiaccess segment.

questions.question: The multicast address for all OSPF routers is:
questions.explanation: OSPF routers use 224.0.0.5 as the all-OSPF-routers multicast address.

questions.question: The BGP Autonomous System Number (ASN) range (as per notes) is:
questions.explanation: As per the notes, the ASN range is 1 to 65535.

questions.question: The default BGP KEEPALIVE interval is:
questions.explanation: The default BGP KEEPALIVE interval is 60 seconds.

questions.question: The final BGP session state, in which UPDATE messages are exchanged, is:
questions.explanation: Established is the final state, where neighbours exchange UPDATE messages.

questions.question: iBGP neighbours are in:
questions.explanation: iBGP runs between routers in the same autonomous system.

questions.question: Route redistribution means:

options.A: Passing routes from one routing protocol or process to another

questions.explanation: Redistribution injects routes learned from one routing protocol or process into another.

questions.question: Route filtering is used to:

options.C: Prevent advertisement or acceptance of certain routes

questions.explanation: Route filtering controls which routes are advertised or accepted.

questions.question: MPLS forwards packets using:
questions.explanation: MPLS forwards packets based on labels instead of looking up IP addresses at each hop.

questions.question: A VPN provides:

options.D: An isolated, secure tunnel across a public network

questions.explanation: A VPN creates an isolated, secure tunnel across a public network.

questions.question: GRE is a:
questions.explanation: GRE is a tunnelling protocol that encapsulates packets inside other IP packets.

questions.question: Which WAN topology is the most fault-tolerant?
questions.explanation: A fully meshed topology has multiple paths between sites, so it is the most fault-tolerant.

questions.question: Why does PortFast help avoid DHCP failure for a PC?

options.B: It gives the PC a static IP
options.D: The port does not wait for the listening and learning states

questions.explanation: Without PortFast the port waits through listening and learning, so the PC's DHCP request can time out; PortFast skips these states.

questions.question: What happens when a PortFast port with BPDU Guard receives a BPDU?

options.B: It goes to err-disabled and stays down until manually re-enabled

questions.explanation: BPDU Guard shuts the port into err-disabled, and it stays down until it is manually re-enabled.

questions.question: UplinkFast speeds up recovery by bypassing:
questions.explanation: UplinkFast moves the backup uplink straight to forwarding, skipping the listening and learning states.

questions.question: Without BackboneFast, switch D in the PPT example waits for:
questions.explanation: Without BackboneFast, switch D must wait for the 20-second Max Age timer to expire before reacting.

questions.question: An inferior BPDU is a BPDU that:

options.B: Is sent only by the root
options.D: Carries worse information than what neighbours already know

questions.explanation: An inferior BPDU advertises worse root information than what the receiving switch already knows.

questions.question: Which command enables PortFast on an interface?
questions.explanation: The interface command spanning-tree portfast enables PortFast.

questions.question: Which command enables BPDU Guard?
questions.explanation: The interface command spanning-tree bpduguard enable turns on BPDU Guard.

questions.question: FTP is not time sensitive because:

options.B: Dropped packets can be resent as it uses TCP

questions.explanation: FTP uses TCP, so lost packets are resent and small delays do not matter.

questions.question: Why is UDP used for the voice stream in VoIP?

options.D: To avoid the processing and bandwidth overhead of TCP

questions.explanation: UDP avoids the overhead of TCP, which suits real-time voice.

questions.question: In QoS, marking means:

options.A: Deciding which packet has priority and labelling it

questions.explanation: Marking labels each packet with its priority so later devices can treat it accordingly.

questions.question: In QoS, scheduling means:

options.B: Serving packets in the order decided by policing

questions.explanation: Scheduling serves packets from the queues in the order decided by the policy.

questions.question: A drawback of traffic shaping is that:

options.C: Memory is required to buffer packets

questions.explanation: Shaping delays excess packets in a buffer, so it needs memory.

questions.question: With WFQ weights of 3, 2 and 1, the router processes:

options.A: Three packets from queue 1, two from queue 2 and one from queue 3

questions.explanation: The weights decide how many packets are served from each queue per round: 3, 2 and 1.

questions.question: In the Leaky Bucket algorithm, when the bucket is full:

options.D: Extra packets overflow and are lost

questions.explanation: When the bucket is full, additional packets overflow and are discarded.

questions.question: In the Token Bucket algorithm, tokens saved during low traffic:

options.B: Allow a burst to be sent later

questions.explanation: Saved tokens can be spent later to send a burst of traffic.

questions.question: Which is the correct difference between the two bucket algorithms?

options.C: Leaky bucket gives fixed output; token bucket allows bursts
options.D: Token bucket gives fixed output; leaky bucket allows bursts

questions.explanation: The leaky bucket gives a constant output rate, whereas the token bucket allows bursts.

questions.question: In the floating static route example, the route to 192.168.1.1 with metric 1 is:

options.A: Installed first; the route via 10.0.0.1 takes over if the first becomes unavailable

questions.explanation: The route with the lower value is installed first, and the backup route takes over if it becomes unavailable.

questions.question: A floating static route protects only against:

options.B: Failure of a directly connected link

questions.explanation: A floating static route reacts only when the directly connected link fails.

questions.question: Why was RIP's broadcast method troublesome for larger networks?

options.D: Updates consume a lot of bandwidth

questions.explanation: Periodic full-table broadcasts consume a lot of bandwidth in larger networks.

questions.question: The OSPF cost of a 10 Mbps link (reference 100,000,000) is:
Why is administrative distance needed?

options.B: Because metrics of different protocols cannot be compared directly

questions.explanation: Different protocols use different metrics, so administrative distance is used to choose between them.

questions.question: If a router learns two paths to a network from the same protocol (OSPF), it compares:
questions.explanation: For paths from the same protocol the administrative distance is equal, so the metric decides.

questions.question: A router learns 20.0.0.0 from OSPF (AD 110) and RIP (AD 120). Which is installed?

options.A: RIP, because it has a higher AD
options.D: OSPF, because it has a lower AD

questions.explanation: The lower AD is preferred, so the OSPF route (110) is installed.

questions.question: In the OSPF cost example, the path via E, F and G (total cost 4) is chosen over the path via B and C (cost 66) because:

options.C: It has the lower total cost

questions.explanation: OSPF picks the path with the lowest total cost.

questions.question: The main difference between IGP and EGP is that:

options.B: IGP works within an AS; EGP connects different ASes
options.C: EGP works within an AS only

questions.explanation: An IGP runs inside one autonomous system, while an EGP connects different autonomous systems.

questions.question: EIGRP routers become neighbours when:

options.A: A hello contains an AS number matching the local EIGRP process
options.C: They are in the same room
options.D: They use the same cable colour

questions.explanation: EIGRP neighbours form when a received hello carries an AS number matching the local process.

questions.question: After becoming neighbours, EIGRP sends update packets:
questions.explanation: Once neighbours are formed, updates are sent in unicast mode to those neighbours.

questions.question: OSPF areas help large networks by:

options.D: Reducing routing table size and limiting changes to an area

questions.explanation: Areas keep routing tables smaller and confine topology changes to the area.

questions.question: In OSPF, traffic between different areas must pass through:
questions.explanation: Inter-area traffic must go through the backbone, Area 0.

questions.question: An ASBR connects:

options.B: An OSPF AS to other autonomous systems or routing protocols

questions.explanation: An ASBR links the OSPF domain to other autonomous systems or routing protocols.

questions.question: The BDR:

options.C: Becomes the DR if the DR fails

questions.explanation: The Backup Designated Router takes over as DR if the DR fails.

questions.question: Type 3 LSA (Summary LSA) is sent by an:
questions.explanation: The ABR generates Type 3 Summary LSAs to describe networks of one area to another.

questions.question: A router with OSPF priority 0:
questions.explanation: A priority of 0 makes the router ineligible for DR or BDR election.

questions.question: In a Point-to-Point OSPF network:
questions.explanation: Only two routers exist on a point-to-point link, so no DR is needed.

questions.question: In an NBMA OSPF network:

options.B: Neighbours are found with multicast hellos
options.C: DR and BDR are elected and neighbours are configured manually

questions.explanation: NBMA does not support multicast, so neighbours are configured manually and a DR and BDR are elected.

questions.question: The OSPF network command includes:

options.D: The network address, inverse mask and area

questions.explanation: The OSPF network command specifies the network address, the inverse (wildcard) mask and the area.

questions.question: The inverse (wildcard) mask for 255.255.255.0 is:
questions.explanation: The wildcard mask is the inverse of the subnet mask: 0.0.0.255.

questions.question: BGP deals with:
questions.explanation: BGP exchanges routing information between autonomous systems.

questions.question: BGP neighbours are:
questions.explanation: BGP neighbours must be configured manually.

questions.question: In BGP, the best path is generally the one that:

options.D: Passes through the fewest autonomous systems

questions.explanation: BGP generally prefers the path with the shortest AS path.

questions.question: The BGP OPEN message contains:

options.B: BGP version, local AS number and BGP router ID

questions.explanation: The OPEN message carries the BGP version, local AS number and BGP router ID.

questions.question: The default BGP hold time is:
questions.explanation: The default BGP hold time is 180 seconds.

questions.question: A BGP NOTIFICATION message is sent when:

options.D: A fatal error occurs and the session is reset

questions.explanation: NOTIFICATION reports an error and the session is then reset.

questions.question: In the BGP Active state, BGP:

options.C: Tries to start a TCP connection

questions.explanation: In the Active state BGP tries to start a TCP connection with the neighbour.

questions.question: By default, iBGP peers within an AS must be:
questions.explanation: By default, iBGP peers within an AS must form a full mesh.

questions.question: By default, eBGP neighbours are assumed to be at most:
questions.explanation: By default eBGP neighbours are expected to be directly connected, one hop away.

questions.question: Protocols do not redistribute routes automatically because:

options.B: They are on the same router
options.D: Each protocol uses a different metric

questions.explanation: Each protocol uses its own metric, so routes cannot be shared without conversion.

questions.question: Which is a valid source of route redistribution?

options.C: Static routes, connected routes and other routing protocols

questions.explanation: Routes can be redistributed from static routes, connected routes and other routing protocols.

questions.question: In "redistribute ospf 2 subnets", the keyword subnets:

options.B: Includes classless subnets, not only classful networks

questions.explanation: The subnets keyword redistributes classless subnets as well as classful networks.

questions.question: Route filtering during redistribution is mainly used to:

options.A: Prevent routing loops and suboptimal routing at multiple redistribution points

questions.explanation: Filtering controls which routes are redistributed, preventing loops and suboptimal routing at multiple redistribution points.

questions.question: Which statement about the MPLS header is correct?

options.A: It is placed before Layer 1 and holds an IP address
options.B: It is placed after Layer 3 and holds a MAC address
options.C: It is placed between Layer 2 and Layer 3 and holds a label, 3 experimental bits, an S bit and TTL

questions.explanation: The MPLS header sits between the Layer 2 and Layer 3 headers and carries a label, 3 experimental bits, an S bit and a TTL.

questions.question: In the MPLS example from the notes, what advantage is shown?

options.A: R4 gets two paths to destination A, whereas normal IP forwarding gives only one least-cost path
options.B: MPLS routers must read IP addresses at each hop

questions.explanation: MPLS allows traffic engineering over more than one path, while normal IP forwarding uses only the least-cost path.

questions.question: Which is a disadvantage of MPLS?

options.D: High cost and poor integration with Internet and SaaS traffic

questions.explanation: Native security, guaranteed bandwidth and QoS are advantages; high cost and poor Internet/SaaS integration are the disadvantages.

questions.question: How does an ISP use MPLS to implement a VPN?

options.B: By isolating the customer's resources and addressing and guaranteeing bandwidth/QoS

questions.explanation: The ISP isolates each customer's resources and addressing and can guarantee bandwidth and QoS.

questions.question: Why is a VPN called an overlay network?

options.A: Because tunnels are laid over the base network

questions.explanation: VPN tunnels are laid over an existing base network, which makes it an overlay.

questions.question: What is special about a packet in a VPN, as per the notes?

options.B: It has an MPLS label only
options.C: It is an ordinary packet with an IPsec header after the IP header

questions.explanation: A VPN packet is an ordinary packet with an IPsec header placed after the IP header.

questions.question: Which statement about the hub-and-spoke topology is correct?

options.A: Spokes talk directly to each other
options.B: Spokes talk only through the hub, which is a single point of failure
options.D: It is the most fault-tolerant topology

questions.explanation: In hub-and-spoke, spokes communicate only via the hub, which is a single point of failure.

questions.question: Which is a drawback of the dual-homed topology?

options.D: It is more expensive and more difficult to implement

questions.explanation: Dual-homing provides redundancy and load balancing but costs more and is harder to implement.

questions.question: Which statement about a fully meshed WAN is correct?

options.A: It connects all sites using multiple virtual circuits and is the most fault-tolerant

questions.explanation: A full mesh connects all sites with multiple virtual circuits and is the most fault-tolerant.

questions.question: With MTU 1500, MSS 1460 plus 20 (TCP) + 20 (IP) + 24 (GRE + IP) bytes gives:

options.C: 1524 bytes, which exceeds the MTU and causes fragmentation

questions.explanation: 1460 + 20 + 20 + 24 = 1524 bytes, which exceeds the 1500-byte MTU and causes fragmentation.

questions.question: With GRE, reducing MSS to 1436 makes the total packet size:
questions.explanation: 1436 + 20 + 20 + 24 = 1500 bytes, which fits the MTU.

questions.question: For 150,000 bytes of data, the number of packets with GRE (MSS 1436) compared with without GRE (MSS 1460) is:
questions.explanation: 150000/1436 is about 104.5, so 105 packets with GRE; 150000/1460 is about 102.7, so 103 packets without GRE.

questions.question: GRE adds which two headers?

options.A: A GRE header and an outer IP header
options.B: A TCP header and a UDP header
options.C: An MPLS header and a VLAN tag
options.D: An Ethernet header and a TOS field

questions.explanation: GRE encapsulation adds a GRE header and a new outer IP header.

questions.question: DMVPN combines:

options.C: GRE tunnels, IPsec encryption and NHRP

questions.explanation: DMVPN combines GRE tunnels, IPsec encryption and NHRP.

questions.question: A multilayer (Layer 3) switch works at:
questions.explanation: A multilayer switch performs both Layer 2 switching and Layer 3 routing.

questions.question: In the BackboneFast example, link A-B fails. What does switch D do?

options.D: Sends an RLQ to A and quickly switches to C as the alternate path

questions.explanation: Switch D sends an RLQ towards the root and quickly moves to the alternate path through C.

questions.question: Which statement about recovery times is correct as per the notes?

options.A: UplinkFast takes about 45 seconds and normal STP about 5 seconds
options.B: UplinkFast and normal STP both take 5 seconds
options.C: UplinkFast takes about 5 seconds and normal recovery about 45 seconds

questions.explanation: UplinkFast recovers in about 5 seconds, while normal STP recovery takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: Which statement about PortFast and BPDU Guard is correct?

options.A: BPDU Guard is normally enabled on PortFast ports to prevent loops from accidental switch connections
options.B: PortFast must be enabled on switch-to-switch links
options.C: BPDU Guard allows BPDUs on PortFast ports

questions.explanation: BPDU Guard protects PortFast edge ports from loops caused by switches connected by mistake.

questions.question: VoIP uses which protocols as per the notes?

options.A: TCP for voice and UDP for control
options.B: UDP for the RTP voice stream and TCP for the control stream

questions.explanation: The RTP voice stream uses UDP, while the control stream uses TCP.

questions.question: An example of policing from the notes is:

options.D: A higher-priority marked packet is allowed to use 10% of the overall bandwidth

questions.explanation: Policing sets limits, such as allowing a higher-priority marked packet to use 10% of the overall bandwidth.

questions.question: How do the two bucket algorithms treat idle time?

options.A: Token bucket saves tokens for later; leaky bucket loses unused capacity
options.C: Leaky bucket saves tokens; token bucket loses them

questions.explanation: The token bucket accumulates tokens during idle time, while the leaky bucket gives no credit for unused capacity.

questions.question: Lack of "reliability" in a flow means:

options.C: Loss of a packet or acknowledgement, leading to retransmission

questions.explanation: Lack of reliability means a packet or acknowledgement is lost, causing retransmission.

questions.question: According to the Daily Quiz, retransmission must NOT be done when the:
questions.explanation: Retransmission is needed for lost, corrupted or unacknowledged packets, not for an error-free packet.

questions.question: According to the Daily Quiz, when the load reaches the network capacity, the delay:
questions.explanation: As the load approaches the network capacity, queues build up and the delay increases sharply.

questions.question: In TCP, the congestion window increases exponentially until a threshold in the:
questions.explanation: In slow start, the congestion window grows exponentially until it reaches the threshold.

questions.question: The switch that becomes the STP root bridge for a VLAN is determined by:
questions.explanation: The switch with the lowest bridge ID becomes the root bridge.

questions.question: Which Cisco feature ensures edge ports do not create Layer 2 loops if mistakenly connected to another switch?
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard disables an edge port that receives a BPDU, preventing loops.

questions.question: Which is TRUE about RIP?

options.B: It does not advertise subnet masks and converges slowly
options.C: It converges in seconds on large networks
options.D: It is a link state protocol

questions.explanation: RIP (version 1) does not advertise subnet masks and converges slowly.

questions.question: How does EIGRP convergence compare with RIP?

options.A: EIGRP converges in seconds where RIP can take minutes

questions.explanation: EIGRP converges in seconds, whereas RIP can take minutes.

questions.question: Which route source has the LOWEST administrative distance among these?
questions.explanation: A static route has an administrative distance of 1, lower than the other options.

questions.question: Which statement about OSPF cost is correct?

options.B: Cost = 100,000,000 / bandwidth in bps, so a 1.5 Mbps link has cost 64

questions.explanation: OSPF cost is the reference bandwidth divided by the link bandwidth; 100,000,000 / 1,500,000 is about 64.

questions.question: Which LSA type pairing is WRONG?

options.C: Type 4 - Summary LSA about ASBR location

questions.explanation: Type 5 is the External LSA, not the Router LSA (which is Type 1).

questions.question: Which OSPF network type uses multicast hellos (224.0.0.5) and elects a DR and BDR?
questions.explanation: Broadcast multiaccess networks use multicast hellos and elect a DR and BDR.

questions.question: The DR and BDR listen on which multicast address?
questions.explanation: The DR and BDR listen on 224.0.0.6.

questions.question: Why does OSPF elect a DR on broadcast networks?

options.A: To increase the flooding of advertisements
options.B: To avoid flooding the network when every router advertises to every other router

questions.explanation: The DR reduces flooding by acting as a central point for LSA exchange.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of BGP session states?

options.A: Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established
options.B: Idle, Active, Connect, OpenConfirm, OpenSent, Established
options.C: Connect, Idle, Active, Established, OpenSent, OpenConfirm
options.D: Established, Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm

questions.explanation: The BGP session states progress as Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm and Established.

questions.question: In which BGP state is the TCP connection established and an OPEN message sent, awaiting a reply OPEN?
questions.explanation: In OpenSent the TCP connection is up and an OPEN message has been sent, awaiting the neighbour's OPEN.

questions.question: In the BGP path example, AS102 prefers AS1, AS2, AS105 because:

options.C: It passes through fewer autonomous systems

questions.explanation: BGP prefers the path through fewer autonomous systems.

questions.question: In the iBGP configuration "neighbor 2.2.2.2 remote-as 100" on a router in AS 100, why is the remote AS the same?

options.A: The neighbour is in a different AS
options.B: iBGP peers are in the same AS

questions.explanation: iBGP peers belong to the same AS, so remote-as equals the local AS.

questions.question: In an eBGP configuration, the remote-as value of the neighbour is:

options.B: Always the same as the local AS

questions.explanation: eBGP neighbours are in different autonomous systems, so remote-as differs from the local AS.

questions.question: How many autonomous systems can a single BGP router be associated with?
questions.explanation: A BGP router belongs to only one autonomous system.

questions.question: When redistributing a static route into RIP, why is "metric 1" used?

options.B: Because RIP uses hop count as its metric

questions.explanation: RIP uses hop count, so a hop-count value such as 1 is assigned to the redistributed route.

questions.question: In "redistribute ospf 1 metric 1 1 1 1 1" under EIGRP, the five values are:

options.C: Bandwidth, delay, reliability, load and MTU

questions.explanation: The five EIGRP metric values are bandwidth, delay, reliability, load and MTU.

questions.question: Why must OSPF routes be given a metric when redistributed into EIGRP?

options.A: EIGRP cannot understand OSPF's cost metric

questions.explanation: EIGRP cannot interpret OSPF's cost, so a metric must be supplied.

questions.question: Which is NOT a valid source for redistribution?
questions.explanation: A MAC address table holds Layer 2 information, not routes, so it cannot be redistributed.

questions.question: Routes learned in EIGRP 100 are shared with EIGRP 200 only if:

options.B: They are in the same VLAN
options.C: A router participates in both processes and redistributes

questions.explanation: A router must run both processes and redistribute between them.

questions.question: Which classification is correct?

options.A: RIP - link state; OSPF - distance vector; EIGRP - path vector
options.B: RIP - distance vector; OSPF - link state; EIGRP - hybrid
options.C: RIP - hybrid; OSPF - distance vector; EIGRP - link state

questions.explanation: RIP is distance vector, OSPF is link state and EIGRP is hybrid.

questions.question: Why is BGP essential for Internet routing?

options.A: The Internet is a collection of interconnected autonomous systems and BGP connects them
options.D: BGP is used only inside a LAN

questions.explanation: The Internet consists of interconnected autonomous systems, and BGP exchanges routes between them.

questions.question: Which WAN topology becomes expensive when many circuits are needed?
questions.explanation: Point-to-point links need a separate circuit per connection, which becomes expensive as circuits multiply.

questions.question: Which statement about QoS is correct?

options.A: QoS increases the physical bandwidth of the link
options.B: QoS removes all lower-priority traffic permanently
options.D: Once traffic is classified, the highest priority traffic is sent first while lower priority traffic waits in a queue
